strategy.title: Fulfil Tri-County's $2,400 purchase order and sell three $650 reconciliation workbooks to auction markets
strategy.why: Tri-County's GM issued a $2,400 PO (2026-11-20, written acceptance); Brain builds it by day 5 and it pays net 20, settling day 25. The remaining $1,600 comes from 3 consignment-reconciliation workbooks at the published $650 listing price, sold to the 240 registered markets, where this offer's own sales paid 14 of 120 contacts; card payout 6 days after order. Total $4,350 settled by day 25 with $44 of direct cost, far inside the $500 capital cap.

stop: No card-paid order at $650 from the first 40 markets by day 10: stop the workbook leg; the price is not established - re-plan it at a researched price (the PO is still delivered and collected).

The workbook price is now correctly held ASSUMED/UNKNOWN with OFFER_AND_PRICE the one link the live test decides. findings: Recomputed: $2,400 + 3 x $650 = $4,350 gross; costs $20 + $24 = $44 <= $500; workbooks needed ceil(1,600/650) = 3. Cash: workbook payouts by day 16, PO day 25. Matches the check trace (collected $4,350 in window).

Threshold carries the target exactly: proof = 3 paid of 40 at $650 by day 10, which with the PO gives $4,350 >= $4,000. Continue branch (1-2 paid -> remaining 200 markets until 3 paid by day 20, settling ~day 26) also lands inside 35. Stop at 0 paid keeps the PO leg.

Ledger note, not blocking: the members block lists 2 Tri-County deals and 7 workbooks as 'standalone arithmetic'; only one PO exists. Steps and cash correctly use 1 PO + 3 workbooks, and that is what the owner acts on, but the member figures should mirror the plan rather than a hypothetical second PO.
Heifer resale correctly excluded ($21,000 tied up vs $500).

strategy.title: Fulfil Tri-County's $2,400 PO and test-sell the $650 reconciliation workbook to auction markets for the remaining $1,600
strategy.why: Tri-County's GM issued a $2,400 PO (2026-11-20, written acceptance); Brain builds it by day 5 and it pays net 20, settling day 25. The remaining $1,600 needs 3 consignment-reconciliation workbooks at $650; that price rests only on other sellers' listing pages (an asking price, not a recorded purchase), so a first $650 card offer to 40 of the 240 registered markets measures it (this offer's own sales paid 14 of 120 contacts); card payout 6 days after order. Total $4,350 settled by day 25 with $44 of direct cost, far inside the $500 capital cap. (Members state each opening's standalone arithmetic, deals = target / price: 2 POs or 7 workbooks; the plan itself takes the one PO that exists plus 3 workbooks, as the steps and cash show.)

validation.proof: At least 3 of the first 40 registered markets pay $650 by card for the workbook by day 10 (with the $2,400 PO this carries the $4,000).
stop: No card-paid order at $650 from the first 40 markets by day 10: stop the workbook leg; the price is not established - re-plan it at a researched price (the PO is still delivered and collected).
continue: 3 or more paid at $650 by day 10: deliver and collect; the target is carried.
1-2 paid by day 10: offer to the remaining 200 markets until 3 paid by day 20, settling by day 26.

disagreements.reason: No conversion is needed: the plan sells this buyer one package and the buyer has already converted — a written acceptance and an EVIDENCE fact record the GM's $2,400 PO dated 2026-11-20. No new buyers are offered.
A one-off purchase order needs its one buyer, who has issued the PO; the plan takes exactly that one deal.

The conversionRates EVIDENCE fact on this card was measured on this offer's own sales to this buyer population: 14 paid orders of 120 contacts (11.7%). The plan needs 3 paid orders, about 26 contacts of the 240 counted markets. The 'close rate not established' text in Brain's basis belongs to the Tri-County PO, not this workbook.

The buyerVolume EVIDENCE fact counts 240 markets on the federal registered-market list with office emails; the plan needs 3 deals (about 26 contacts at the measured 14/120), about 1% of the counted buyers buying once.
